structure.problem: Acme Retail’s CMO wants one dashboard for the Shopify site and the new iOS app. Two agencies propose two separate GA4 Accounts so ‘nobody messes up the other platform.’
structure.solution: Create one Account → one Property → web + iOS (+ Android later) data streams. Share key events and explorations in that property. Use access roles if agency separation is the real worry.
structure.takeaway: Unify platforms in one property when they are one business; use permissions—not duplicate accounts—for access control.

dimensions-metrics.problem: A PM builds a Looker Board mixing ‘Item name’ next to ‘Sessions’ and insists the totals ‘must match Ads.’ Numbers look chaotic in the meeting.
dimensions-metrics.solution: Separate labels (dimensions) from counts (metrics). Rebuild the view as Item name × Item views / purchases, and keep session metrics in a session-scoped report.
dimensions-metrics.takeaway: Every trustworthy chart starts by naming what is a dimension vs a metric—and respecting scope.

key-events.problem: Paid media asks to ‘turn on conversions’ for newsletter_signup, but the event never appears in Admin → Events.
key-events.solution: Implement/collect the event first (GTM or gtag), verify in DebugView, then mark it as a key event. Only then link/import to Ads if needed.
key-events.takeaway: A key event is a flag on an event that already exists—not a substitute for tracking.

reports.problem: After a Friday deploy, leadership says ‘GA4 is broken’ because Life cycle reports still look empty an hour later.
reports.solution: Open Realtime (and DebugView on a test device) to confirm hits. Explain standard report latency. Keep the deploy rollback decision tied to Realtime proof, not overnight reports.
reports.takeaway: Realtime confirms collection; standard reports can lag—don’t declare failure from the wrong screen.

explore.problem: Analysts keep rebuilding the same ‘purchasers in last 14 days’ filter inside every Explore, and Ads wants that list for remarketing.
explore.solution: Use a Segment for one-off analysis. Publish an Audience when the set must be reusable or shared with linked Google Ads.

scopes.problem: A custom dimension ‘membership_tier’ was registered as Event-scoped but the app sets it once as a user property. Explore shows mostly ‘(not set)’.
scopes.solution: Align registration scope with how the value is sent. Prefer a user-scoped custom dimension / user property for durable membership tier.
scopes.takeaway: Wrong scope is one of the most common sources of ‘GA4 is lying’ meetings.

attribution.problem: Brand search looks heroic under last-click; Paid Social looks useless. Social wants budget restored.
attribution.solution: Show the same conversions under Data-Driven (or model comparison) and discuss assisted paths and lookback windows. Don’t debate budgets from a single last-click export.
attribution.takeaway: Always name the attribution model when you tell a budget story.

campaign-tracking.problem: A partner QR code ‘should be campaign-tagged’ but GA4 shows Direct spikes when people scan it.
campaign-tracking.solution: Inspect the redirect chain—query parameters were stripped. Fix the redirect to preserve UTMs (or use a tagged short link that keeps them).
campaign-tracking.takeaway: UTMs only work if they survive every hop to the landing page.

advertising.problem: Finance compares Google Ads UI conversions to GA4 Advertising and declares one tool wrong.
advertising.solution: Reconcile definitions: conversion actions, attribution windows, click vs view, timezone, and linking status. Expect differences; hunt mismatches, don’t force equality.
advertising.takeaway: Cross-platform totals rarely match 1:1—align definitions before aligning opinions.

governance.problem: Office Wi‑Fi and a payment gateway inflate sessions and referrals before Black Friday reporting.
governance.solution: Define internal traffic rules and unwanted referral exclusions, document owners, and note that filters are not retroactive for past weeks.
governance.takeaway: Governance is configuration plus ownership—not a one-time checkbox.

bigquery-api.problem: Explore samples on a huge date range; the data science team needs item-level joins for a margin model.
bigquery-api.solution: Enable BigQuery export and query events there. Use the Data API for lighter scheduled report pulls; Measurement Protocol only for true server/offline hits.
bigquery-api.takeaway: Pick the pipe for the job: UI, Data API, or BigQuery—not one tool for everything.

ga360.problem: Legal wants an EU-only analytics view, while the exec team wants one rollup across two brand properties.
ga360.solution: Discuss 360 subproperty (filtered child of one source) vs roll-up (combine multiple sources). If not on 360, approximate with separate properties, BQ views, and strict access control.
ga360.takeaway: Subproperty filters one source; roll-up combines many—don’t mix the words in stakeholder decks.

consent.problem: After CMP launch, paid channels claim ‘GA stopped’ because observed conversions dropped.
consent.solution: Verify Consent Mode wiring in GTM/gtag, check granted vs denied behavior in DebugView, and explain modeled conversions / lower fidelity when consent is denied.
consent.takeaway: Consent changes fidelity—measure the wiring before blaming the media mix.

signalsads.problem: Someone enables Google Signals in a rush hoping for ‘free cross-device magic,’ then rows disappear due to thresholding.
signalsads.solution: Align with privacy/legal first. Enable Signals deliberately, teach User-ID as first-party identity for logins, and explain thresholds on small slices.
signalsads.takeaway: Signals are powerful and constrained—enable with policy, not FOMO.

setupassist.problem: A new hire trusts a green Setup Assistant checklist even though Realtime is empty after a tag change.
setupassist.solution: Treat Setup Assistant as a reminder list. Re-open it after new streams or Ads links, but always verify hits in Realtime/DebugView independently.
setupassist.takeaway: A checklist is not proof of collection.

eventparams.problem: The team invented 60 custom event names for clicks that already map to recommended events, and standard reports look sparse.
eventparams.solution: Prefer automatically collected → recommended → custom. Rename/consolidate where possible; register only the custom dimensions you truly need.
eventparams.takeaway: Fit Google’s taxonomy before inventing your own dialect.

enhanced-measurement.problem: Product enables every Enhanced Measurement toggle; form_start floods the property and key-event ideas get silly.
enhanced-measurement.solution: Disable noisy toggles, configure site-search params correctly, and implement true submit events in GTM when EM form events aren’t enough.
enhanced-measurement.takeaway: Enhanced measurement is a starting kit—not a reason to skip intentional tracking design.

debugview.problem: QA says ‘nothing in DebugView’ after a GTM publish, while Realtime occasionally blips.
debugview.solution: Enable debug mode on the test browser, confirm the GA4 tag fires to the correct Measurement ID in Preview, then inspect parameters in DebugView.
debugview.takeaway: DebugView only sees debug-flagged traffic—configure the test device on purpose.

user-id.problem: CRM wants cross-device journeys and proposes sending email addresses as user_id.
user-id.solution: Refuse PII. Emit a stable irreversible first-party ID after login, clear it on shared-device logout, and document the identity policy.
user-id.takeaway: User-ID is first-party identity—never raw personal data.

cross-domain.problem: Sessions restart when users move from brand.com to checkout.partner.com, wrecking funnel reports.
cross-domain.solution: Configure cross-domain measurement / linker for both domains, test client IDs across the hop, and review referral exclusions for the gateway.
cross-domain.takeaway: Without linker setup, a domain hop often means a new session.

predictive.problem: Growth asks for churn probability audiences on a two-week-old property with thin purchase volume.
predictive.solution: Check eligibility prerequisites. If greyed out, wait for qualifying examples; don’t invent fake scores in spreadsheets for Ads.
predictive.takeaway: Predictive metrics appear only when the property earns them with data.

channel-groups.problem: Paid Social lands in Referral because of sloppy UTMs; the channel meeting becomes a blame session.
channel-groups.solution: Fix tagging conventions first, then adjust custom channel rules (mind first-match order) and set the Primary group intentionally.
channel-groups.takeaway: Channel groups interpret tags—they don’t forgive chaotic UTMs.

gtag-gtm.problem: Engineering hardcodes gtag; marketing installs a second GTM container ‘just for pixels,’ doubling page_view.
gtag-gtm.solution: Pick an ownership model: either governed GTM as the system of record or documented gtag—not both firing the same base hits. Deduplicate and add publish approvals.
gtag-gtm.takeaway: Two install paths without governance means duplicate hits and duplicate arguments.
